positive_definition: Computes a single scalar metric over the refunds input: rows whose refund_id (or equivalent unique refund-event identity) has already appeared at an earlier position in input order are counted as replay rows; the replay row count is divided by the total number of refund rows to yield the replay rate. Computation only reads and counts rows; it does not alter, drop, or cap any event. Exposed as metric_tool with compute_metric(orders, refunds) and output_name refund_replay_rate.
exclusions: Does not remove or deduplicate replay rows or return a filtered event list (that is refund-event-dedup-v1).
Does not accumulate or cap refund value per order against original gross merchandise value (that is cumulative-refund-cap-v1).
Does not compute ordinary refund rate or refund-to-sales ratio (that is refund_rate).
Does not rank categories or produce per-group breakdowns (that is category_ranking).
Does not modify input rows, amounts, or field values in any way.
reason: The task requires a replay-rate scalar keyed to repeated refund_id occurrences, but existing tools only expose daily_net_sales, refund_rate, and category_ranking, and existing plugins only deduplicate or cap refund events. Neither deduplication nor capping reports a replay proportion, so the expected result refund_replay_rate is unavailable; a minimal metric_tool computing replay rows over total refund rows fills exactly this gap.
